chunks: And in it it is narrated that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except in the well-known matter.
And it is the testimony to Allah, His Messenger, and the Imam.
For if he testifies to Allah and His Messenger but does not testify to the Imam, Satan assists him so that he may disbelieve.
And if he testifies to Allah and the Imam but does not testify to the Messenger, Satan assists him so that he may disbelieve.
And if he testifies to the Messenger and the Imam but does not testify to Allah, Satan assists him so that he may disbelieve.
But if he testifies to Allah, His Messenger, and the Imam, Satan does not have power over him.
ai.seo_question: What is the 'well-known matter' that gives Satan authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish the theological necessity of *Imamah* alongside *Tawhid* and *Nubuwwah* as the triad of faith. This highlights the Shia doctrine that Satan's influence is neutralized only when the believer acknowledges the divine authority of the Imams, ensuring spiritual security from misguidance.
